messages:
OncallBot: :rotating_light: Paging: sev-2 latency SLO breaches on cont-batch path in us-west-2 for multiple tenants. p95 ~ 420ms (target 120ms), p99 ~ 1.8s. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/contbatch/latency?orgId=1 :rotating_light:
Sam: ack, I'm on it. jumped in the dashboard, saw a big skew in tail.
Jess: thanks. any recent rollout to batch scheduler? I pushed a scheduler tweak last night but it was small.
Sam: there was a canary of fairshare weights rolled at 01:10 UTC, might be related. canary id: rollout-2026-03-14-0110
Marta: I'm seeing a correlated increase in streaming stalls (client-side stall events) on routes that use continuous batching + streaming. logs show repeated requeues in the batch scheduler.
Jess: requeues + mixed seq lengths = bad combo. long seqs hold the KVcache and block batch flushes.
Sam: agreed. reproducing locally with a simple load: 80% short (<=128) and 20% long (>=4096) sequences causes tail blowups.
Leo: quick mitigation options: 1) disable cont-batch feature flag for affected routes 2) force scheduling fairness back to old weights 3) cap max_batch_size temporarily 4) route long sequences to dedicated non-cont-batch workers.
Sam: trying option 1 first: toggling ff via admin API
Sam: ```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/featureflags/cont_batching/routes/toggle \
  -d '{"routes": ["/v1/generate","/v1/chat"], "enabled": false}'
```
OncallBot: Feature flag toggle accepted (request id ff-8891). Propagating to proxies.
Marta: I pushed a quick rule to the routing table to isolate long_sequences - added header-based route: `x-redwood-seq-len >= 2048 -> dedicated-legacy` so long ones don't enter cont-batch.
Jess: good call. also lowering max_batch_size to 16 on cont-batch nodes as a safety cap.
Sam: applying cap via configmap patch now:
```bash
kubectl -n inference patch configmap cont-batch-config -p '{"data":{"max_batch_size":"16"}}' || true
kubectl rollout restart ds/cont-batch -n inference
```
Leo: I'm scaling up dedicated fallback pool by +4 replicas to handle drift.
R&D-Eval-Bot: Running online evals against canary -> 3/5 evals show latency improvement, 2/5 show steady throughput drop.
Sam: initial numbers: after ff toggle and cap, p95 down to 150ms, p99 down to 320ms on impacted routes. still monitoring.
Marta: still seeing occasional stalls on streaming clients at ~10-15/min, digging into request traces.
Jess: trace snippet (correlated with requeue): `scheduler.go:241: requeue due to batch lock timeout (held by seq id 0x7f3a)`
Sam: note for followup: need smarter per-request routing based on seq_len histogram, and scheduler should avoid head-of-line blocking by prioritizing small sequences when latency SLOs are at risk.
Leo: I'll open a ticket to revert the canary weights and add an explicit fairness test to CI.
Sam: handoff to night oncall @Marta in 30m. current mitigation: cont-batch disabled for user-facing routes, max_batch_size=16, long sequences routed away, +4 dedicated replicas. impact: customer-facing p95/p99 back within SLO for 90% tenants, a minority still seeing intermittent stalls.
Marta: taking over. will keep watchers for 2 hours, will escalate if p99 > 600ms for >5m.
Jess: thanks all. postmortem action items: (1) rework scheduler fairness algorithm, (2) add mix-workload unit tests, (3) improve feature-flag rollout checks for latency regressions, (4) traffic-aware max_batch_size autoscaler.
Sam: adding links to dashboards/alerts in the incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.internal/pages/contbatch-2026-03-14
